title: CrFeVW<i>X</i> (<i>X</i> = Ta or Ti) High-Entropy Alloy: A Theoretical and Experimental Comparative Investigation on Phase Stability.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Equiatomic or near-equiatomic mixtures of elemental Cr, Fe, V, W with X = Ta or Ti (i.e., CrFeVWTa and CrFeVWTi), prepared from high-purity elements as powders or pieces for melting.
recollection.intervention: Guess: A combined theoretical-experimental study: (i) ab initio/DFT assessments of mixing enthalpies and short-range order plus CALPHAD/thermodynamic modeling to map phase stability vs temperature; (ii) arc melting (multiple remelts) and casting, followed by homogenization (≈1100–1250 C) and isothermal anneals; (iii) characterization by XRD/Rietveld, SEM-EDS/EBSD, TEM/SAD to distinguish A2 vs B2 and identify intermetallics; and DSC/DTA to detect ordering or decomposition.
recollection.structure: Guess: The Ta-containing alloy forms predominantly a single-phase bcc (A2) solid solution at high temperature, with possible weak B2-type ordering on cooling, whereas the Ti-containing alloy decomposes into a bcc matrix plus intermetallics, notably Laves (C14/C15, e.g., TiCr2-type) and possibly σ phase (Cr-Fe-W rich), with intergranular precipitation after annealing.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Configurational entropy stabilizes a bcc solid solution at high T for both, but enthalpic/chemical effects dominate on cooling. Strong negative pairwise mixing enthalpies involving Ti–Cr (and Ti–W) drive Laves formation and promote σ in the Ti variant, while Ta exhibits weaker driving forces for intermetallics and better solubility with Cr/Fe/V/W, maintaining A2 (and modest A2→B2 short-range order) over a wider T range. VEC and size misfit trends favor bcc; however, the Ti alloy’s enthalpy asymmetry leads to phase separation and ordering at intermediate temperatures as predicted by CALPHAD/DFT free-energy landscapes.
recollection.results: Guess: CALPHAD/DFT predict A2 stability for CrFeVWTa across a broad temperature window (≈900–1500 C), with a low-temperature A2→A2+B2 tendency, whereas CrFeVWTi shows narrower single-phase bcc stability and enters bcc+Laves (and minor σ) fields on cooling below ≈1000–1100 C. Experimentally, after homogenization at ≈1200 C, CrFeVWTa is ≳85–95 wt% A2 bcc with lattice parameter a ≈ 2.93–2.98 Å; CrFeVWTi shows multiphase microstructures (≈40–70% bcc with ≈20–40% Laves and 5–15% σ, depending on anneal). Microhardness is lower for the Ta variant (≈500–600 HV) and higher for the Ti variant (≈650–800 HV) due to intermetallic strengthening. DSC reveals a subtle ordering exotherm (A2→B2 SRO) in the Ta alloy around 700–900 C, and stronger exo/endotherms associated with intermetallic precipitation/dissolution in the Ti alloy.

score.note: The recollection is largely a speculative account of a different workflow. It substitutes DFT/CALPHAD, arc melting, homogenization, and annealing for the actual MD/hybrid MD–MC simulations, ball milling, and spark-plasma sintering. It also reverses the key phase behavior: the Fe2Ta C14 Laves phase occurred in CrFeTaVW, while CrFeTiVW had two bcc-type phases rather than the proposed Ti-based Laves/σ decomposition. The proposed chemical mechanism likewise contradicts the reported strong negative Fe–Ta mixing enthalpy. Reported phase fractions, temperatures, hardness, and lattice parameters are unsupported or inaccurate, and the actual thermal-diffusivity result is absent.
